product: K9 self propelled howitzers, Chunmoo K239 rocket artillery, air defense and missiles, aircraft and missile engines plus MRO, space launch vehicles (Nuriho) and satellites, marine gas turbines, batteries and energy storage, armored vehicles.
demand: Strong and broadening: European rearmament, Middle East restocking, US Army cannon modernization and Asian programs. Land systems backlog was KRW 38.3T at Q2 2026, about 4.7 years of work, with Q2 revenue up 47% yoy.
pricing_power: Strong on export, weak at home. Brokers estimate Q2 export operating margin in the 35 to 39 percent range against high single digit domestic, helped by a favorable won and K9PL mix, while domestic mass production runs at mid to high single digit margins.
competition: Rheinmetall, KNDS, Nexter, BAE Systems, Elbit, Turkey Roketsan and China Norinco abroad; LIG Nex1, Korea Aerospace Industries and Hyundai Rotem at home. Localization and technology transfer, not headline price, now decide tenders.
team: Hanwha Group controlled. Vice Chairman Kim Dong-kwan is widening oversight into space and AI as group results and orders grow; Baek Ki-bong leads the PGM2 missile business. Management guides to localization led growth and is buying a KAI stake.
market_strategy: Localization: build local production, JV and technology transfer to win and keep orders. Australia and Romania up to 80 percent local content, Spain with Indra, US via Hanwha Defense USA and Philly Shipyard, plus EU local content rules. Extending from Eastern Europe into Western Europe, the US and the Middle East.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue KRW 9.293T up 47% yoy and operating profit KRW 1.3655T up 59%, first above KRW 1T; export mix margin 35-39%; backlog KRW 38.3T about 4.7 years; dated orders Croatia EUR 411.8M 2026-09-10 and US K9MH 2026-08-24.
bear: FY2025 net income fell 38.9% to KRW 1.40T, levered FCF minus KRW 1.18T, debt/equity 78.7%; stock about 38% below 52-week high and YTD plus 8.5% vs KOSPI plus 68%; Poland concentration; 2026-09-23 engine tender drew no bids.
falsifier: Q3 2026 ground systems operating margin reported below 10% (versus 35-39% export margin), or a Poland K9 EC3 award slipping past 2026-12-31.
web_what_changed: Record Q2 2026 on 2026-07-31: revenue KRW 9.293T up 47% yoy, operating profit KRW 1.3655T up 59%, first quarter above KRW 1T. Then US Army K9MH prototype award 2026-08-24, Spain K9 execution contract with Indra 2026-09-01, Croatia 18 Chunmoo for EUR 411.8M signed 2026-09-10, and a Hanwha Aerospace and KAI KF-21 missile MOU on 2026-09-23.
web_not_known_yesterday: Dated 2026-09-23 and reported 2026-09-24: Hanwha Aerospace signed an MOU with Korea Aerospace Industries to integrate a domestically developed long range air to air missile on the KF-21, ahead of the missile system development award. Hanwha has also been building a KAI stake, reported between about 7 and 15 percent, making it a major shareholder.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Almost entirely volume and mix, not price. Q2 export revenue was KRW 1.2324T, up 14% yoy, on Poland K9 and Chunmoo, Egypt and Middle East deliveries; domestic rose 27% on Chunho and Cheongeom. Broker notes estimate export operating margin near 35 to 39 percent versus high single digit domestic, so profit growth is export mix plus volume.
web_suppliers: Related suppliers are Hanwha Systems (radar and command systems) and Hanwha Ocean (shipbuilding), plus partners Indra in Spain, Generation 5 Holding for local K9 production, Thales and Northrop Grumman. Constraint evidence: the GTF RSP engine venture lost KRW 10.2B in Q2, a Daejeon plant accident disrupted production, and engine and guided weapon supply remains tight.
web_customers: Republic of Korea armed forces, Poland (largest export customer, over half of exports), Egypt, Australia, Norway, Estonia, Finland, Croatia (18 Chunmoo, EUR 411.8M, 2026-09-10), Romania K9 about KRW 1.4T, Spain via Indra, and the US Army K9MH MTC prototype worth about USD 260M with options. Land systems backlog was KRW 38.3T in Q2, about 4.7 years; Poland concentration is the key risk.
web_who_loses: European incumbents Rheinmetall, KNDS and Nexter lose artillery and air defense share as K9 and Chunmoo take Poland, the Nordics, Croatia, Spain and Romania. In the US, BAE Systems and Elbit lose MTC ground. Domestically LIG Nex1 and Korea Aerospace Industries face a stronger Hanwha; Turkey Roketsan and Chinese exporters lose tenders.
web_contradicting_evidence: Stock YTD plus 8.5% versus KOSPI plus 68%, and about 38% below the 52 week high of KRW 1,713,000. FY2025 net income fell 38.9% to KRW 1.40T, levered free cash flow was minus KRW 1.18T, debt to equity 78.7%. The Q2 beat relied on listed units Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Systems; a Daejeon plant accident hurt output; Middle East talks slipped; a 2026-09-23 aircraft engine localization tender drew no bids.
web_if_management_right: Order momentum converts: Poland K9 EC3, Romania, Spain, Saudi MNG and the US MTC programme of roughly 500 guns and KRW 10T. FY2026 revenue about KRW 32.2T and operating income about KRW 4.76T, EPS about KRW 48,100, supporting the KRW 1.65M to 1.67M consensus target, about 63% above the last close.
web_if_management_wrong: Margin breaks first. If Poland EC3, Saudi and US awards slip, or localization and technology transfer dilute the 35 to 39 percent export margin, EPS upgrades reverse and the premium multiple (PBR 4.4x, forward PE about 23x) compresses. A Nuriho launch failure would also damage the space story. Cracks show first in ground systems operating margin, then in the share price.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Hanwha Systems for radar and command systems and Hanwha Ocean for shipbuilding and US MRO, plus the Korean K9 supply chain and propellant or ammunition makers such as Poongsan. Beyond the group: LIG Nex1, Hyundai Rotem, HD Hyundai Heavy and Samsung Heavy from US MASGA shipbuilding, and local partners Indra and Generation 5 Holding.
